text: Let us pray. Heavenly Father, Lord, we thank you for the opportunity to bring the tithes and offering to your store. Lord, we pray that you may multiply it and use it to the further extension of your kingdom. In Jesus name we pray. Amen. It is now time to take up the little lamb's offering. I invite the little ones, and it will be followed by a story as well by David.

Good morning everyone. Are you still waiting? Microphones can help. Everyone can hear me. Who would like to pray for us? Let's pray. Amen. That was the Lord's prayer. Beautiful. I want to start off a story that happened in my life about ten or eleven years ago.

I want to start off by reading a verse to you. This is from the Gospel of Luke. Luke chapter 18 and verse one. It says, Then Jesus spoke a parable, which is like a story to the people that were listening to him. And the point of this story was that people should always pray and not become discouraged or give up praying.

I was studying in America about ten years ago. America is a lot bigger than our country South Africa. It is very big. This was during summer time, and when we have winter they have summer and when we have summer they have winter.

This was around June or July and as part of my school we had to go throughout Michigan, knock on people's doors, talk to them about Jesus, and try to get them to buy books about Jesus and the Bible. That work can get scary because people are sometimes not nice. They can slam the door, call the cops, or you can get chased by dogs.

It is still a really nice thing to do. You meet all kinds of people that you would not meet any other way. One day we had to be outside from eleven in the morning until half past seven at night. On some days things would go very well and one after another people were buying your books.

You felt blessed and that God was very close. People were smiling and allowing you to pray for them. On this particular day I did not sell even one book. I knocked on about a hundred doors and every person said they were not interested. Near the end of the day I began to feel very sad and wondered if I had made God angry.

That was not true, but it was the thought that came to my mind. There was something inside me that said, Keep on praying. Keep on praying. Don't stop praying. And so I did. We were driven to another neighborhood and it was the last place we would knock on doors before going home.

I wondered if I was going to end the day with nothing. I prayed a special prayer in my heart and said, Lord, it has been a very long day and I have really been trying. Can you give me some kind of experience? I want to be used and see someone blessed because of what I am doing. I knocked on the door and was told to go away.

My heart began to sink. At the next door the same thing happened. I was afraid people would call the cops on me. I was just about to give up when I had this thought: Keep on going. Keep on praying. And so I did. There was one last door and I had about ten minutes left.

I said, Lord, please do something. I walked up to the door, knocked, and there was no answer. I was about to walk away when I heard something. A lady was rubbing her eyes as if she had just woken up. My friends had the police called on them for waking people up.

I came up to the door and started to tell her why I was there. I had books about God and Jesus. Her eyes got bigger and she asked, Who sent you? I said I worked with an organization and tried to explain myself. Then a man came up behind her.
